book.title: The Penguin Book of Independent Crosswords, volume 1

clue.text: Dog finds fish alien

parts.note: the bass is a common sea fish
ET is the film's extra-terrestrial, crossword shorthand for an alien

explanation.surface: A dog sniffing around discovers a strange, unfamiliar fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset is a short-legged hound breed with long ears, so it is one kind of dog.

clue.text: One province or another around North

indicators.note: around says one word is placed so that it surrounds the other letter

parts.note: another province, taken as a region or sphere
N is the compass abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: Someone vaguely gestures at a map: this province or that one, somewhere round the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words mean a field of activity: ARENA is one province, and AREA, the other, wraps round N.
explanation.definitionFit: A province can mean a sphere of activity or concern, which is exactly what an arena is in its figurative sense.

clue.text: Such as travels by air is safe, getting over a flutter!

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting over means sitting on top of what follows

parts.note: sound as in safe and sound, unharmed
a wave of the hand is a flutter

explanation.surface: Air travel is declared safe once a passenger gets past a nervous flutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travels by air' suggests flying, but a sound wave travels through the air as vibration.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound waves are vibrations carried through the medium of air, so they literally travel by air.

clue.text: Sprat's last to admit of fat

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the end of Sprat
to allow is to admit or permit

explanation.surface: Echoes the rhyme of Jack Sprat, who could eat no fat.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Sprat of the nursery rhyme could eat no fat, which makes 'fat' look part of the story rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow is rendered animal fat, used for candles and soap, so it is a kind of fat.

clue.text: Officer's cane, mine, returned to personnel

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so this word is read right to left

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
staff are the personnel of an organisation

explanation.surface: An officer's walking stick, which belonged to me, is handed back to the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is the metal-tipped staff carried as a badge of office by a court officer, hence an officer's cane.

clue.text: B R employee's a persistently offending driver?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a railway worker who checks fares, BR being British Rail
second meaning, whimsical: a motorist who keeps picking up parking or speeding fines

explanation.surface: Asks whether a British Rail worker is a habitual motoring offender.
explanation.walkthrough: BR was British Rail, the old nationalised railway; the 's is read as 'is'. The question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway worker who checks and gathers passengers' tickets has this job title; a driver forever fined literally amasses tickets.

clue.text: Timely play with words involving a cult

parts.note: a pun is a play on words

indicators.note: involving in its old sense of entangling or twisting up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A timely piece of wordplay that drags in some religious cult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involving' looks like a container signal, but nothing fits inside the play on words; read it as entangling the letters that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Timely and punctual both describe something that happens on time, at the proper moment.

clue.text: Mark depicts Judas throwing away gold?

indicators.note: throwing away says some letters are discarded from the word before

parts.note: Judas betrayed Jesus, the archetypal betrayer
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Mark's gospel shows Judas casting aside the silver he was paid.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like the gospel writer, but it is the definition, a distinguishing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing feature or characteristic, and a mark can mean such a characteristic.

clue.text: Fellow's just horrible!

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for Fellow, as in FRS
rightful means just or fair

explanation.surface: An exclamation that some chap is simply dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' reads as 'simply', but it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightful and horrible both describe something dreadful, shocking or very unpleasant.

clue.text: Party, in US, is concerning the host

parts.note: re means concerning, as in business letters
a publican runs a pub and plays host to drinkers

explanation.surface: An American party is all about whoever is hosting it.
explanation.walkthrough: A publican is the landlord of a British pub, the host behind the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The Republicans are one of the two main political parties in the United States, so a member belongs to it.

clue.text: Parched and 'arassed, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: harried, meaning harassed, with the dropped H of Cockney speech

explanation.surface: Someone thirsty and flustered, in a Cockney voice.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'arassed signals the dropped H: harried said without its H sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid land or air is extremely dry, which is what parched means.

clue.text: Help a few, being generous

parts.note: to lend a hand is to help
some means a few

explanation.surface: Helping out a handful of people is the kind thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome gift or sum is a large, liberal one, so the word can mean generous.

clue.text: Cross, type half cut, incorporating design on metal

indicators.note: incorporating means taking something into the body of the word
half cut says half of the word is chopped off

parts.note: taken as written, then halved
to etch is to cut a design into metal with acid

explanation.surface: An irritable, drunk-sounding sort of fellow works at engraving metal.
explanation.walkthrough: Half cut is British slang for tipsy, a disguise for halving the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy describes someone irritable and short-tempered, the same mood as being cross.

clue.text: Some Thais are about, here

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters run backwards
some means only part of the following words is taken

parts.note: the letters run straight through the two words

explanation.surface: Some people from Thailand are around, where they belong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here' is the definition by context: the place where Thais are found.
explanation.definitionFit: Thailand lies in this continent, so 'here', said of where Thais are, points to it.

clue.text: "Twist" — a dance, and a crazy one

parts.note: to screw is to twist
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: The Twist, a dance craze of the sixties, and a wild one at that.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make Twist look like the dance; it is a verb meaning to turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwball is an eccentric or crazy person, so the phrase for a mad individual fits.

clue.text: Grade and label 'Secret'

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sort into categories or ranks
second meaning: mark official documents as restricted

explanation.surface: Sorting papers and stamping them as secret.
explanation.definitionFit: To grade is to sort into categories, and governments mark restricted documents as confidential, the other sense of the verb.

clue.text: Very brief spell on low, temporary bed

parts.note: a moment, as in two shakes
down means low, as in feeling low

explanation.surface: A quick nap lying on a low makeshift bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In two shakes' means in a moment, so a shake is a very short time.
explanation.definitionFit: A shakedown is an improvised bed made up on the floor or a sofa for a night.

clue.text: Bridge call, signal suggesting guarantee of entry

parts.note: in bridge a player who declines to bid calls pass
to give the word is to give the signal

explanation.surface: A bid at the bridge table that signals a guaranteed way in.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret word given to a sentry or lock grants admission, so it secures access.

clue.text: Does bank in collapse give one that sinking feeling?

definitions.text: Does bank in collapse give one that sinking feeling?

parts.note: surface reading: a bank going bust, a financial crash
setter's reading: a skydiver banking in the air drops unimpeded before the parachute opens

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a bank failure and its dread; the answer is a plunge through the air, where a parachutist banks and literally sinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Free fall is unchecked descent under gravity, and the phrase also names a sudden uncontrolled collapse of prices.

clue.text: Friend? Entirely unknown

parts.note: all means entirely, as in all alone
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: Is this a friend, or a complete stranger?
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is someone on your side, a supporter or partner, like a friend.

clue.text: Cold on tender chest?…

parts.note: C stands for cold, as on a tap
to tender is to offer, as in a tender for a contract

explanation.surface: A cold settling on a sore chest, running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender chest' suggests a sore ribcage; tender is a verb and chest the definition. The dots link to the next clue's chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffer is a strongbox for valuables, a type of chest.

clue.text: Bad beer causes strokes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old word for thin, sour or poor-quality beer
second meaning: sweeping blows or hits

explanation.surface: Drinking rotten ale brings on a stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Swipes was slang for weak, inferior beer, and swinging blows aimed at something are also called by this word.

clue.text: …Dad's wrapping chest in wind-proof garment

indicators.note: wrapping means one word encloses the other like packaging

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
an ark is a chest or box, as the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Father bundles up his chest against the weather in a warm coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots tie this to the chest of the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded jacket designed to keep out wind and cold.

clue.text: Cryptic secret I cracked, finding nothing in it

indicators.note: in it says a further piece goes inside the jumbled letters
something cracked is broken apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A solver boasts of cracking a cryptic secret only to find nothing inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' sounds like crossword talk but is the definition, meaning obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by an initiated few, so it is obscure, hidden or mysterious.

clue.text: Church anthem lacks appeal as opener for jazzmen

indicators.note: lacks means the word that follows is missing from the one before

parts.note: the introit is the chant sung at the start of Mass
it means sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: A church anthem without allure serves as a warm-up for a jazz band.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening passage of a piece of music before the main tune, as jazz bands play.

clue.text: Piano tune for duet

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, meaning softly
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A piano melody written for two players.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet involves two performers, and a couple of anything is a set of two.

clue.text: Destitute types, off-colour

parts.note: destitute of means lacking, out of
sorts are kinds or types, and in printing a sort is a piece of type

explanation.surface: Penniless characters looking unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase came from printing: a compositor out of sorts had run short of a piece of type.
explanation.definitionFit: To be out of sorts is to feel slightly unwell or grumpy, just as off-colour means a little ill.

clue.text: German river's engulfed thin shrub

indicators.note: engulfed means swallowed up, so one word sits wholly inside the other

parts.note: the Oder runs along the German–Polish border
lean means thin

explanation.surface: A German river in flood has swallowed a spindly bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is an evergreen flowering bush of the Mediterranean, so it is a type of shrub.

clue.text: US author has to score 'Over there…'

parts.note: a run is a score in cricket or baseball
yon is old or dialect for over there

explanation.surface: An American writer must set to music the song 'Over There'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over There' is a famous First World War American song, which makes score look like writing music.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon Runyon was an American writer of Broadway stories, the basis for Guys and Dolls.
